title: India's First Bullet Train to Run in Last Quarter of 2027, Surat-Vapi First
excerpt: Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw says the first high-speed service will open between Surat and Vapi, with the full Mumbai-Ahmedabad corridor following in phases and track trials of the indigenous B28 trainset expected by mid-2027.
body:
• India's first high-speed rail service will commence in the last quarter of 2027, Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said on Friday, with the Surat-Vapi section of the Mumbai-Ahmedabad corridor opening first.
  • The full 508 km corridor to Mumbai will follow in phases. Fares, a timetable and a booking channel have not been announced.
  • Construction progress as of September: 456 km of pier work and 371 km of viaduct completed, civil work finished at eight stations, and the first body frame of the indigenous B28 trainset complete and in structural testing.
  • For travellers: nothing can be booked yet. The first service is a Gujarat section, not a Mumbai-Ahmedabad through journey, and track trials are expected only by mid-2027.
Announced, not yet operating: The minister has confirmed the first section (Surat-Vapi), the opening window (last quarter of 2027) and phased opening of the rest of the corridor. As of November 20, 2026, no launch date within that quarter, timetable, fares or booking channel has been announced.

India's first bullet train service will begin in the last quarter of 2027, and the first section to open will run from Surat to Vapi in Gujarat, Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said on Friday in a post on Substack, reported by PTI via the Deccan Herald. The full corridor to Mumbai will follow in phases, he added.

The Friday update refines the timeline given earlier this month, when reports pointed to an August 2027 opening for the same Surat-Vapi section. The minister's account now places the first passenger service in the last quarter of the year, after track trials of the trainset expected by mid-2027.

How much of the corridor is built

Talking about the pace of construction, Vaishnaw said that as of September, 456 km of pier work and 371 km of viaduct construction have been completed on the 508 km Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail corridor. Six lakh noise barriers have been installed along a 299 km stretch, and 9,300 overhead equipment masts have been installed across a 206 km viaduct, he wrote.

Civil work has been completed at eight stations, with architectural finishing work under way, and work is in progress at all three rolling stock depots, at Sabarmati, Surat and Thane. Four mountain tunnels have been excavated. In Maharashtra, the corridor runs through a 21 km tunnel, of which 7 km passes under the sea beneath Thane Creek — India's first undersea rail tunnel. Five kilometres of the 21 km tunnel have been excavated using the mountain tunnelling method, and two tunnel boring machines launched in July 2026, from Vikhroli and Sawli, are at work on the rest. Each machine has a cutterhead 13.6 metres in diameter and weighs over 3,000 tonnes, Vaishnaw said.

The train itself: B28 first, B35 next

The services will be worked by India's first indigenous bullet trains. ICF and BEML are manufacturing the B28 trainset, designed for 280 kmph, the minister said. The first body frame is complete and is undergoing structural testing, and track trials are expected by mid-2027. A faster B35, designed for 350 kmph, is the next step.

According to information from the Ministry of Railways reported by Urban Acres, the roughly 202-metre B28 will have eight coaches — four motor cars and four trailer cars — and is designed to carry an estimated 557 passengers, including two designated spaces for Divyangjan and persons with reduced mobility. Seven coaches will have standard-class seating in a 3x2 configuration and one executive-class coach will have 2x2 seating. Its planned operational speed is 249 kmph. The minister has said the Mumbai-Ahmedabad journey would take 1 hour 58 minutes, compared with eight to nine hours by road today; those travel-time figures are the minister's claims and will depend on the operating pattern and the sections available when services begin.

"The fixed infrastructure is being indigenised too. All major transformers of the high-speed electrification system, the cross arms on the masts, the ground, protection and feeder wires: all are being manufactured in India," Vaishnaw stated. Earlier reporting by Hindusthan Samachar put overall completion of the project at nearly 80 per cent, with 12 stations planned along the corridor.

Why a 2017 project is opening in 2027

Vaishnaw addressed the delay of almost a decade since the project was first announced in 2017. The project could not start in Maharashtra for close to two and a half years because state permissions and land acquisition were pending, he said. "Then COVID took away two more years. Full construction began in earnest in 2021," he said. "So, when critics ask, 'where is the bullet train', the honest answer is: serious construction is just five years old. And look at what five years have built," he added.

Before planning your trip

  • There is no booking channel, fare or timetable yet — the minister's announcement names none, as of November 20, 2026.
  • The first service covers Surat-Vapi only. A through Mumbai-Ahmedabad journey follows later, in phases, on dates not yet announced.
  • Track trials of the B28 trainset are expected by mid-2027 and must be completed before passenger services begin.
  • Journey-time figures (1 hour 58 minutes for Mumbai-Ahmedabad) are the minister's claims for the completed corridor, not a published schedule.
